what: An oscillator made of sixteen sine waves added together, so you choose which overtones are present.
how: Every note is a fundamental sine plus overtones at 2x, 3x, 4x... its frequency. Here the first sixteen are mixed for you. TILT sets how fast they fall in loudness, ODD/EVEN favours one kind, and COMB spotlights one region of overtones. A sine has none; a saw has them all.

ins.pitch: Pitch in octaves (1 volt per octave, 0 is middle C). Patch KEYS' pitch here.

knobs.tune: Shifts the pitch in semitones, -24 to 24 (two octaves down to two up), added to the pitch input.
knobs.tilt: The slope of the overtones, -1 to 1. Low (negative) values keep more overtones for a brighter tone; high (positive) values make the sound closer to a sine.
knobs.oddeven: Weights the even or odd overtones, -1 to 1. Positive removes the even ones (hollow, like a clarinet); negative removes the odd ones.
knobs.comb: Picks out a band of overtones, 0 to 1. At 0 all overtones are used; raised, it favours a narrower region that moves up as you turn it.

try: Patch KEYS' pitch into ADDITIVE's pitch, ADDITIVE's out through a VCA and ENV into OUT. Hold a note and move TILT and ODD/EVEN to hear the overtones change.
